change_areas: Bounded production and content parsing before large allocations; completeness propagated through publications and audit measurements.
Content/configuration generation checks and uncached failures prevent observed stale or partial publications.

Bounded post and metadata cache priming preserves candidate-read failure detection and avoids per-row database queries; an observed N+1 regression was repaired and given a permanent native release check.
Native REST response handling respects WordPress final serialization rather than applying byte validators to a pre-transformation body.
Configuration writes compare expected stored bytes and roll back only still-owned values; failures and concurrent writers remain visible.

Automatic retired MCP cleanup and static/translation defaults preserve concurrent authorized saves and explicit choices through exact observed-value replacement; conflicting cleanup remains retryable.
Per-path static ownership storage, resumable legacy migration, connection-bound fences and bounded lifecycle reconciliation.
Authoritative database state, option leases, queue claims, upgrade checkpoints and Cloudflare authorization transactions.
RSS UTC dates, XML characters, canonical and query aliases, multisite behavior and old-permalink notifications.
Bounded admin probes, stale-response fencing, overlapping-operation controls and diagnostic analytics exclusion.
Local release validation now covers additional native database cases, browser security, source guards and harness self-tests.
WordPress-compatible literal prepared SQL retains exact-byte compare-and-swap and connection-bound fences; uninstall inventory queries use adjacent fixed templates.
Raw and decoded input ceilings preserve valid protocol bytes; Identity search checks method, capability and nonce before bounded query/cursor parsing.

Stored-template inspection uses scoped prepared theme membership and immediate query-failure capture. It reads raw content without rendering dynamic blocks or invoking block hooks; ordinary WordPress query filters are now allowed to affect results.
Every mandatory runtime case requires typed native option-CAS and stored-template fixture success after cleanup, in addition to publication cache-priming checks.

phpunit.qualification: The full suite passed after fixing a strict test SQL adapter. Native HTML cases use the preserved verified Core 7.1 HTML API. A later native-only malformed-fence fixture correction passed syntax and 20 matcher checks; the final mandatory gate follows this checkpoint.

native_fault_cases.qualification: Ten fixtures ran on both engines and cache modes under WordPress 7.1/PHP 8.2.33. Automatic-settings checks use native connections and SQL/cache/hooks; translation detection uses a fixture constant. Four small block-theme checks do not establish full-site capacity. MySQL malformed empty fences return false with an explicit empty-lock-name error while MariaDB returns zero; both preserve exact stored bytes. The corrected fixture checks typed results rather than requiring identical engine error behavior.

native_publication_smoke.scope: Early and deep sitemap requests in a 10,000-primary-record mixed corpus across native/Redis and plugin cache off/on.
native_publication_smoke.qualification: The two 201-post fault probes run on MariaDB with native/Redis caches and restore saved state in finally. HTTP counts are 16 counted and 8 warmup samples; one cold and one counted warm observation per condition do not establish robust latency. The corpus contains 5,500 published posts, not 10,000 selected public posts. This does not replace the four-size matrix.

website.remaining_reason: The public audit checkpoint must bind the fresh exact-ZIP performance evidence before this guide review can be completed.
website.scope_note: Final exact-commit import, editorial review, website build and live verification are separate required release steps. Current source review is not deployment approval.

relay.health: HTTP 200, protocol 1, status ok, all five rate-limit bindings reported present.
relay.configuration: Recorded bindings and runtime metadata unchanged; existing secret binding retained without reading its value.
relay.qualification: Commit and local bundle hashes are associated with the Wrangler deployment receipt; deployed module bytes were not independently downloaded. Health/control-plane checks do not establish a live OAuth round trip or production concurrency.
relay.logs: Invocation logging disabled in the submitted configuration; historical logs and independent log sinks were not audited or deleted.

source_safety.qualification: These individually reviewed inherited scopes are not zero annotation-blind findings. The installed official Plugin Check is a separate zero-findings gate.

request_boundaries.qualification: Real administrator/Subscriber sessions and session-bound nonces cover the Identity AJAX boundary on both databases and cache modes. URI/header assertions assign superglobals after native WordPress bootstrap; they are not live HTTP transport tests. No claim covers every controller or browser interaction.

installed_plugin_check_diagnostic.qualification: One early single-site installed-ZIP diagnostic passed before the native-only malformed-fence fixture correction. This is not the mandatory six-case release matrix.

performance.state: All four sizes and fresh ownership collected and independently reviewed; costs and incomplete outcomes retained.
performance.cache_matrix: Native versus Redis object cache, each with the plugin cache setting off and on.
performance.same_fixture_not_identical_work: The corrected link resolver finds real fixture edges missed by the baseline; do not treat both graph analyses as identical work.
performance.static_measurement: One bounded sync invocation per mode. Files, ownership and options are not reset to empty between modes; a later terminal slice is not an independent cold full-publication benchmark.
performance.invalid_samples: Retain timeouts, missing metrics, invalid responses and incomplete operations; suppress percentiles for any group containing invalid requested samples.
performance.controlled_limits: Six shared CPU cores and per-process address-space ceilings, plus a sampled aggregate RSS and workspace watchdog. This is not a kernel-enforced aggregate cgroup memory guarantee.
performance.sampling: Sequential HTTP requests: three counted cold and 20 counted warm samples per endpoint/cache mode; the first warm request is excluded. These descriptive percentiles are not concurrent-throughput or production-tail guarantees.
performance.cache_qualification: Cold clears application caches, not database buffers or OS caches. The plugin cache setting does not disable independent discovery caches. Synthetic distinct client addresses avoid rate-limit interference.
performance.response_qualification: Valid means expected status, nonempty body and protocol shape. Successful bodies were not retained for semantic URL-set, privacy or byte-equivalence comparison; fixture host ports differ.
performance.query_qualification: The slowest SELECT samples and selected execution plans are not a complete query-frequency or write-latency trace.
performance.resource_qualification: Six shared CPU cores; per-process address-space ceilings of 6 GiB for the database, 1 GiB for Redis and each of up to three PHP processes, and 256 MiB for the helper; sampled aggregate RSS and workspace watchdogs at 12 GiB and 90 GiB. Instrumentation overhead and shared-host effects remain.
performance.corpus: Deterministic bulk SQL creates the named number of primary records across public/private/draft/future post types, plus attachments at 10% and revisions at 5%. The 1M fixture therefore contains 1,150,000 wp_posts rows. Bulk seeding does not measure importer or WordPress hook throughput.
performance.baseline: Cybermaps 8.0.1 at the fixed commit and ZIP hashes above. Current terminal-state rules are applied to historical static results so pending publication is not counted as complete.

retained_observations.status: measured extra query and cold latency cost retained
retained_observations.description: Cold RAG uses 568 native or 555 Redis queries versus 70/57 baseline, 498 additional queries in each mode. Cold p95 is 0.199–0.261 seconds versus 0.142–0.181 across the four conditions. Same 887-byte response size does not establish semantic equivalence. No universal query reduction is claimed.

retained_observations.status: observed latency spikes; cause not isolated
retained_observations.description: Native-cache/plugin-cache-on LLMS-TLDR warm p95 is 0.3797 seconds versus 0.0607 baseline (6.26x), driven by two of 20 samples. Cold search-hit p95 is 0.4960 versus 0.1328 (3.74x), driven by one of 3. Aggregate query-time spikes coincide; SELECT-only samples do not establish their cause.

Candidate graph resolves 649 edges among 700 resources versus baseline 0/700. Homepage depth is unavailable. Static files and continuation state carry across modes; successful later slices are not independent first-publication timings.

retained_observations.status: measured extra query and cold latency cost retained
retained_observations.description: Cold RAG uses 682 native or 669 Redis queries versus 70/57 baseline: 612 additional queries per mode. Cold p95 ratios are 1.36–2.53x. Response byte size matches, but full success bodies are not retained for semantic comparison.

retained_observations.status: observed latency costs; source attribution not isolated
retained_observations.description: Native/plugin-cache-off warm LLMS p95 is 0.5523 seconds versus 0.0991 (5.57x), with three query-time spikes. Native/plugin-cache-on cold LLMS is 1.627 versus 0.487 seconds (3.34x); native/plugin-cache-off warm search-miss is 0.4201 versus 0.1633 (2.57x). Saved SELECTs do not establish the cause.

retained_observations.status: bounded page work confirmed; queries exceed baseline
retained_observations.description: Native/plugin-cache-off cold early/deep sitemap counts are 79/74 versus baseline 46/46. Page 1 and page 3 are distinct at this size. Maximum counts across modes are 83/78. This corroborates bounded post/metadata reads rather than one query per URL; it does not imply every query is optimal.

retained_observations.status: substantial measured fresh-selection cost; improvement opportunity remains open
retained_observations.description: Warm Redis search-miss p95 is 0.820/0.745 seconds versus 0.065/0.076 baseline (12.63x/9.85x); hits are 0.378/0.337 versus 0.080/0.096 (4.73x/3.51x). Representative candidate SELECT costs dominate recorded SQL time. PublicationQuery forces fresh full-row selection and captures immediate SQL errors; the baseline uses ordinary query-result reuse. This supports substantial database-cost attribution, not every wall-time difference or optimality. Any optimization must preserve freshness, eligibility and SQL-error outcomes; this matrix does not test mutation freshness.

Warm Redis/plugin-cache-off deep sitemap p95 is 0.571 seconds versus 0.173 (3.30x). A representative LIMIT 54000,2000 selection costs 0.296 seconds, with a separate 0.049-second count. The retained baseline trace lacks that expensive selection; it is not an exhaustive SQL log.

retained_observations.status: cold query and latency cost retained
retained_observations.description: Cold RAG has 612 additional queries per mode, with p95 1.69–2.18x baseline. Warm result reuse does not establish cold scan cost or correctness after content changes.

retained_observations.status: substantial fresh-selection cost retained; optimization opportunity remains open
retained_observations.description: Warm Redis search-hit p95 is 2.612–2.640 seconds versus 0.0859–0.0884 baseline (29.86–30.41x), and search-miss is 7.092–7.172 versus 0.0696–0.0751 (94.49–103.11x). Representative fresh SELECTs dominate recorded SQL time. Disabling native query-result reuse preserves immediate SQL failure detection; these measurements do not establish optimality, every wall-time cause or mutation freshness.

retained_observations.status: bounded query counts with deep-page database cost retained
retained_observations.description: Warm Redis/plugin-cache-off deep sitemap p95 is 1.823 seconds versus 0.509 (3.58x). Representative LIMIT 544000,2000 selection costs 1.174 seconds plus a 0.385-second count. Native/plugin-cache-off early/deep query maxima remain 79/65. Redis/plugin-cache-on cached deep-page p95 is 0.530 versus 0.446; its representative count dominates SQL rather than a fresh candidate selection.

retained_observations.status: cold query and latency cost retained
retained_observations.description: Cold RAG uses 682 native or 669 Redis queries versus 70/57 baseline, 612 extra queries in every mode. Cold p95 is 11.525–15.317 seconds versus 8.059–8.353 across the four conditions. Warm cache reuse does not establish cold scan efficiency, semantic body equivalence or correctness after content changes.

Native/plugin-cache-off warm search-hit p95 is 5.343 seconds versus 2.375 baseline. Native/plugin-cache-on cold sitemap-index p95 is 11.844 versus 7.706. Saved query traces and shared-host measurements do not isolate every source of those wall-time differences.

request_accounting.qualification: Includes all requested records across four sizes and four modes. Warmups are excluded from counted percentiles; skips remain requested work. Interrupted 10k records are preserved separately and not merged.

ownership.state: Three scoped synthetic operations complete and independently reviewed
ownership.qualification: One synthetic forced-flush metadata-write observation per size on native object cache. The 1k and 10k candidate observations are slower, while 5k is faster. Queries increase from 7N+14 to 8N+15, approximately 14.3%; submitted SQL text bytes decrease. This is not a latency distribution, physical I/O measurement, independent readback of every saved row, populated legacy migration, filesystem publication or total first-publication benchmark.

cleanup.state: Owned runtimes, networks, temporary paths and driver processes observed absent after completed collection. Interrupted pause cleanup remains separately retained.
cleanup.qualification: This concerns task-owned resources; unrelated historical resources are preserved.

n_plus_one_disposition.status: Narrow sitemap per-row query regression repaired and independently corroborated across all four sizes.
n_plus_one_disposition.qualification: Cold child-page query counts stay bounded by page work rather than one query per URL. Counts still exceed baseline; search/RAG/deep-page costs and incomplete operations remain. No blanket performance pass.

accepted_limits.description: A worker-created request-cache object with a shared nested mutable object can be evicted after a caller changes that nested object. The caller object retains its change. No wrong public response or persistent mutation was demonstrated; no first-party producer of this shape was established. Universal preservation of arbitrary extension objects is not claimed.

accepted_limits: Cooperative byte, time and memory checks do not interrupt a blocked database/cache call or guarantee an arbitrarily large row fits memory.
Publication output ceilings and bounded static slices remain deliberate limits; a partial result is not reported as completed.
Diagnostic redaction is best effort; support bundles require local review before sharing.

Metadata cache hooks run earlier in 100-ID batches while cache additions are suspended; arbitrary hook cache-write side effects and original invocation cadence are not universally preserved. A batch count is not a metadata byte ceiling.
Third-party plugins, external caches/CDNs and production traffic differ from the controlled fixtures.

Stored-template reads allow ordinary WordPress query filters to affect their results. Raw stored-content inspection does not establish compatibility or equivalent behavior for arbitrary third-party query filters.
candidate_status: Source/native/performance audit checkpoint complete, including independent evidence review. All measured costs, failed observations and remaining limits are retained. Mandatory exact-ZIP release validation, publication and website deployment are separate pending steps.

open_findings.disposition: Retained without a code fix; exact behavior and limits are documented in accepted_limits.

checkpoint_scope: This immutable source and performance audit checkpoint precedes the mandatory final release gate. It records only completed evidence available at this checkpoint; final runtime validation, publication and live-website completion are recorded separately.

release_handoff.state_at_checkpoint: Mandatory release gate, publication and website deployment pending. No approval or completed release is claimed by this source checkpoint.

historical_checkpoint.qualification: The earlier checkpoint and its d086 performance results are retained as history. They are not substituted for current 112ed89e measurements.
